/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
import importlib.util
for name in ['pypdf','pdfplumber','fitz','PIL']:
 print(name, bool(importlib.util.find_spec(name)))
from pypdf import PdfReader
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('PAGES',len(r.pages))
from pathlib import Path
out=Path('tmp/pdfs')
out.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
for i,p in enumerate(r.pages):
 text=p.extract_text()
 (out/f'page-{i+1:02d}.txt').write_text(text)
(out/'manuscript.txt').write_text('\\n\\n'.join(f'=== PAGE {i+1} ===\\n'+p.extract_text() for i,p in enumerate(r.pages)))
print((out/'manuscript.txt').read_text())
PY"

strengths: The paper offers a useful conceptual simplification: generate an approximate virtual correspondence and reuse established five-point and P3P solvers for the difficult 4p3v configuration. The mean-based variant is particularly appealing because it requires neither training nor additional feature geometry. This methodological contribution has value independently of benchmark superiority.

The experiments support competitive performance against dedicated 4p3v methods. Across 10,000 real image triplets, the learned variant improves AUC@5 degrees over homotopy continuation from 43.25 to 47.14 on Sacre Coeur and from 19.45 to 21.34 on St. Peter’s Square. The much simpler mean-based variant achieves results close to homotopy continuation.

The supporting evidence includes synthetic experiments, 452,500 projected correspondence triplets for studying the mean-point strategy, controlled noise experiments, and a two-view extension evaluated on 9,900 image pairs. Training the learned predictor entirely on synthetic data and evaluating on real imagery provides useful evidence of transfer.

The manuscript clearly explains the constraint count and acknowledges that its solvers are approximate, including their nonzero errors on noiseless inputs. Its candid finding that conventional 5pt+P3P generally remains preferable is useful practical guidance. The supplement supplies meaningful architecture, loss, and training details.
weaknesses: The demonstrated practical advantage is primarily simplicity, rather than improved accuracy and speed together. In Table 1, the learned solver takes 38.50 and 14.13 seconds, versus 2.59 and 2.46 seconds for 5pt+P3P, while generally delivering slightly worse accuracy. The mean-based solver also does not outperform homotopy continuation in the reported accuracy or runtime measures. Consequently, the efficiency and state-of-the-art claims need qualification.

The evaluation does not establish accuracy of the complete three-camera reconstruction. Both RANSAC scoring and reported pose errors use the 1–2 and 1–3 essential matrices, with translation evaluated only by direction. These measures are insensitive to the relative lengths of the two baselines, an additional quantity required for joint three-view geometry. No relative-scale, aligned camera-center, or joint reprojection evaluation closes this gap.

The operating range of the approximation remains insufficiently characterized. Figure 2 establishes favorable average behavior, but does not show how often individual virtual matches have large errors or how these depend on perspective distortion, depth variation, and baseline. The real robust-estimation experiments cover two landmark scenes, and no controlled outlier-ratio study establishes the proposed smaller-sample advantage. The broader applicability claims therefore remain preliminary.

Important experimental details are missing despite the useful network supplement: RANSAC thresholds, confidence and iteration limits, local refinement, and selection or filtering of multiple solver solutions are not adequately specified. These choices affect both accuracy and runtime, making the comparisons harder to reproduce and interpret. Accuracy-versus-runtime curves would also better contextualize the learned solver’s substantial overhead.

A smaller technical clarification concerns permutation invariance in Section 3.2. Although the Set Transformer is permutation invariant, normalization selects the first and second correspondences, and virtual-point initialization uses the first three. The complete pipeline therefore does not inherit invariance automatically. This is a correctable claim-level issue and does not undermine the central contribution.
